scope: Client presentation CPU work only. Geometry, material, display resolution and authoritative gameplay rules are preserved.

measurement.method: Wall-clock microsecond totals for repeated function calls in one scene, three timed passes after one warm-up pass. These are microbenchmarks, not frame rates or whole-game CPU/GPU times.
measurement.limitations: Measurements ran in a shared development environment. Some isolated paths are unchanged or slower; these totals do not establish a whole-game speedup or a smartphone frame rate.

changes: Redraw the battle HUD only when its displayed state, input feedback or layout changes.
Cache viewport-dependent input rectangles and panel style; refresh the cache on viewport resize.
Reuse arrow/orb meshes and materials across shot visuals, keeping the same geometry and material values.
Avoid repeated idle weapon/camera transforms and unchanged remote-player label assignments.
Reuse snapshot-generation tracking and stale-player lists instead of rebuilding per-snapshot collections.

scope: Weapon/camera transforms over normal and strong attacks
Remote-player transforms, animation poses and labels
presentation_before_after.comparison: Transforms use the same approximate-equality tolerance as the regression script; remote figure poses and input rectangles compare equal. This is not an RGBA pixel comparison.

right_half_touch.method: Actual viewport.push_input ScreenTouch and ScreenDrag events, with fixed finger ownership and simultaneous movement/look input.
scope: Right-half non-button press owns the look finger
Separate ownership for move, attack, jump, skill and Home buttons
Reset on resize, portrait, cancellation, focus, Home, death and spawn
Ignore emulated mouse events with device -1
Window mouse capture, mouse camera and mouse attack
